Topics · One God, one message

Can I be sure I'm right and still respect others?

A prophet tells his opponent: we or you are guided. The Quran's manners: self-testing, fairness, a good word.

Part 1 of 3

﴿قُلْ مَن يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ قُلِ ٱللَّهُ ۖ وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَـٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ٢٤ قُل لَّا تُسْـَٔلُونَ عَمَّآ أَجْرَمْنَا وَلَا نُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ٢٥ قُلْ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَنَا رَبُّنَا ثُمَّ يَفْتَحُ بَيْنَنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَهُوَ ٱلْفَتَّاحُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ٢٦﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?" Say, "Allāh. And indeed, we or you are either upon guidance or in clear error." Say, "You will not be asked about what we committed, and we will not be asked about what you do." Say, "Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the Knowing Judge."[1232]

Translator's notes

[1232] Literally, "Opener," i.e., He who decides and lays open all matters in truth and justice and who opens the way to victory, success, relief, knowledge and understanding.

Quran · Saba 34:24-26

Translation

Are there any among the vanities of the nations that can cause rain? Or can the sky give showers? Aren’t you he, Yahweh our God? Therefore we will wait for you; for you have made all these things.

Original · Hebrew

הֲיֵ֨שׁ בְּהַבְלֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ מַגְשִׁמִ֔ים וְאִם־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם יִתְּנ֣וּ רְבִבִ֑ים הֲלֹ֨א אַתָּה־ה֜וּא יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ וּ֨נְקַוֶּה־לָּ֔ךְ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתָ אֶת־כָּל־אֵֽלֶּה׃

Jeremiah · 14:22

World English Bible

Many think respect means being sure of nothing, or that being sure means contempt. These verses do a third thing. The Messenger, confident in what he holds, is told to say: either we or you are on guidance, or in clear error. He does not give up his claim; he places himself under the same test. Then he goes further: you will not be asked about what we did wrong. Confidence and fairness can meet, when the last verdict is God's.

A question for you

What does it mean to you for someone to put themselves under the same test?

If you sayThat they are not sure
ThenIt can seem so. But this comes from someone confident. Real confidence may be what does not fear a test.
If you sayThat they are fair
ThenThat fairness is what makes people listen.
If you sayI could not do that with my faith
ThenUnderstood; it touches what you love. Yet this manner comes from the Quran itself.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَا تَسُبُّوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَسُبُّوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَدْوًۢا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ ۗ كَذَٰلِكَ زَيَّنَّا لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ عَمَلَهُمْ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِم مَّرْجِعُهُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And do not insult those they invoke other than Allāh, lest they insult Allāh in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have made pleasing to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them about what they used to do.

Quran · Al-An'am 6:108

A guide, on finding a man who has lost his way, brings him back to the right path—he does not mock and jeer at him and then take himself off. You also must show the unlearned man the truth, and you will see that he will follow. But so long as you do not show it him, you should not mock, but rather feel your own incapacity.

Stoic writings · Golden Sayings 63

Epictetus, Golden Sayings (Crossley)

Being sure gives you no right to insult. This verse forbids reviling what people call on besides God. It protects even those you disagree with from the tongue of one who feels right. The reason is practical: revile what someone holds sacred, and they will revile what you hold sacred, in ignorance. Insult harms what you love. The verse adds that each nation's work was made pleasing to it, the same picture as each party rejoicing in 30:32.

A question for you

Which is harder for you: not mocking, or defending the dignity of someone who differs?

If you sayNot mocking
ThenIt begins with a brief silence before the word.
If you sayDefending their dignity
ThenThat leads to the next part: fairness and kindness.

Part 3 of 3

﴿لَّا يَنْهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَـٰتِلُوكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَـٰرِكُمْ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمْ وَتُقْسِطُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Allāh does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allāh loves those who act justly.

Quran · Al-Mumtahanah 60:8

Translation

“If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him again. If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him. You shall surely help him with it.

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֣י תִפְגַּ֞ע שׁ֧וֹר אֹֽיִבְךָ֛ א֥וֹ חֲמֹר֖וֹ תֹּעֶ֑ה הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֶ֖נּוּ לֽוֹ׃ כִּֽי־תִרְאֶ֞ה חֲמ֣וֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ֗ רֹבֵץ֙ תַּ֣חַת מַשָּׂא֔וֹ וְחָדַלְתָּ֖ מֵעֲזֹ֣ב ל֑וֹ עָזֹ֥ב תַּעֲזֹ֖ב עִמּֽוֹ׃

the Torah (Exodus) · 23:4-5

World English Bible

Is it enough not to do harm? The verse goes further: God does not forbid you from showing goodness and fairness to those who have not fought you over religion. The word for goodness is a large one, the same used for honouring parents. It closes: God loves the fair. Respect here is no cold tolerance. It is a deed God loves. Being sure of what you hold does not excuse you from such goodness; it should make you first to practise it.

A question for you

What one word or act would show respect without giving up your conviction?

The same in the other books

Translation

For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same? If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?

ἐὰν γὰρ ἀγαπήσητε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, τίνα μισθὸν ἔχετε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ τελῶναι τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν; καὶ ἐὰν ἀσπάσησθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὑμῶν μόνον, τί περισσὸν ποιεῖτε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ ἐθνικοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;

the Gospel (Matthew) · 5:46-47
